summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held positions at Butler University (attested 1986), the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and served as a Guest Scholar at Soka University.

Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley (attested 2014).

Daniel Boucher is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. He studied at Indiana University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, Ludo Rocher, and Gregory Schopen, later serving as Associate Professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008).

Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale University (1963) and Harvard University (1965, 1972) before holding a faculty post at the University of Washington from circa 1972 to 2017.

Daniel Coit Gilman (1831–1908) studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Humboldt University. He served at Yale (~1856–1872), UC Berkeley (~1872–1875), and was president of Johns Hopkins (1875–1901), the American Oriental Society (1893–1906), and Carnegie Institution (~1901–1904).

Daniel Cozort (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~1982–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins and taught at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2021).

Daniel Dubuisson (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique and the University of Lille, and held a post at University Lille-III (~1981–2015).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1916–1999) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University (~1932–1941) under Willard Van Orman Quine and Walter Eugene Clark, later serving as Harvard's Wales Professor of Sanskrit (~1958–1983; emeritus ~1983–1999).

Daniel John Gogerly (1792–1862) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as chairman of the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (~1838–1862) and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845–1862).

Daniel L. Overmyer (1935–2021) was a sinologist and scholar of religion who studied at the University of Chicago (~1966–1973). He held posts at Oberlin College (~1970–1973) and the University of British Columbia, including Department Head (~1985–1993) and Professor (attested 2010).

Daniel M. Stuart is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, mentored by Alexander von Rospatt. In 2017, he was attested as Assistant Professor at the University of South Carolina.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Stuart Capper, Jr. is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Veidlinger (born 1970) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999), and held a post at California State University, Chico (2006).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia. In 2010, he held instructor posts at the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.
Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and ethno-anthropology, having earned her PhD from the University of Siena. In 2004, she was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned doctorates from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.
Danielle Feller is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1938–1947), and served as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China (~1953–1992).

Daud Ali (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at William & Mary (~1982–1986) and the University of Chicago (~1988–1996), and held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~2009) and SOAS University of London (attested 2013).
